statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail sits in the low band because CME equity futures are closed and the last observed tape was orderly, while Stress stays high on the pre-FOMC rates and energy backdrop and on a weekend that added a fatal Strait of Hormuz strike and Houthi control of a second chokepoint.
recommendation: Tail remains below the caution threshold, so the mapped state is EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. One narrow window is flagged: the 22:00-00:00 UTC Globex weekend reopen, where two days of unpriced Gulf headlines meet thin liquidity and the mapped state there is WATCH.
headline: Nasdaq-100 closed and orderly into a hawkish Fed week, with a fatal Hormuz strike and Houthi control of Bab el-Mandeb framing the Sunday reopen
body: CME equity futures are shut until 22:00 UTC, so no live NQ price path exists at assessment time. The last observed tape is Friday's: the Nasdaq-100 closed at 29,368.44, up 0.91%, inside a 29,313.51-29,473.12 range and about 105 points below the session high, so the index was not pinned at an extreme, while VIX fell 11.21% to 15.84. That structure is orderly and retracement-friendly, which keeps Tail in the low band. The backdrop is tighter than the tape suggests. Treasury yields sit at 4.95% on the 10-year, 4.56% on the 2-year and 5.37% on the 30-year; WTI is near $100.05 after a roughly 9.7% weekly gain and Brent traded above $105 during the week; and markets price roughly an 86% chance of a 25 basis point hike at Wednesday's FOMC under Chair Kevin Warsh, a call on which Goldman Sachs and J.P. Morgan openly disagree. Equities near record highs with VIX under 16 against that stack is a thin cushion, which is why Stress is high while Tail is not. The weekend added two developments pulling in opposite directions. An Iranian commercial vessel was struck early Sunday near Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, killing one and wounding several, after UKMTO reported a projectile strike, fire and crew evacuation late Saturday; separately, Houthi forces have taken Bab el-Mandeb islands and the Red Sea port of Mokha, putting a second chokepoint in play while a US naval blockade has already redirected about 100 ships. Against that, Iran meets Gulf states and Iraq in Salalah on Monday to present an Oman-brokered framework for a temporary shipping corridor, with maps to be filed with the IMO. Iranian officials have said plainly that the framework does not reopen the strait and that no agreement is expected to be signed. Conflicting signals of that kind widen dispersion rather than establish a one-way path, so they are scored as Stress and Confidence rather than Tail. The single concentrated risk point in the coming window is the 22:00 UTC Globex reopen, where all of this reprices into thin Sunday-evening liquidity; Tail enters the watch band for those two hours as a conditional gap allowance, then eases on the base case that Asian trade restores two-way flow. Monday's US calendar holds only 3-month and 6-month bill auctions at 15:30 UTC, leaving the session headline-driven with crude as the main transmission channel. Further out, Wednesday's FOMC and Friday's record options expiration, which Citadel Securities has sized at roughly $9.6 trillion of exposure running into September 18, shape the rest of the week. Shared Finviz cross-asset context was collected at 16:40 UTC with partial status and is older than the 90-minute freshness bound, so it was treated as stale and not relied upon; the assessment rests on independently verified sources.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding published hours were available and uniformly green with the mapped state EA_ON. Tail held flat at 6 from late Saturday through the overnight hours, then drifted up from 05:00 UTC to 17 by 15:00 UTC as the weekend ran toward the futures reopen, dipping to 16 and returning to 17 in the final hour. Stress rose steadily from 52 to 72 as the pre-FOMC rates and energy backdrop accumulated, the dominant mode stayed normal throughout, and Confidence held near 86 before stepping down to the low 70s in the last two hours as the weekend evidence gap widened.
outlookSummary: The window splits into three phases. Until 22:00 UTC the CME equity complex is closed and no price path can form, so Tail holds in the low band and rises only as a forward allowance into the reopen. The 22:00-00:00 UTC Globex reopen is the single concentrated risk point, where two days of Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb and Fed-expectation news reprice into thin liquidity; Tail enters the watch band for those two hours as a conditional gap allowance rather than an observed move. From the Asian hours onward the base case is absorption of the gap and a return to two-way trade, with Tail decaying toward 16 and modest conditional upticks at the European open and the 13:30 UTC US cash open. Monday's US calendar holds only routine bill auctions, so residual risk is headline-driven, with crude the main transmission channel and the Salalah meeting an unresolved checkpoint that Iranian officials have already said will not reopen the strait. Stress stays in the high band throughout because the underlying tension - a live hike debate, a 10-year near 5%, crude near $100 and two contested chokepoints - is unresolved before Wednesday. Confidence starts in the solid band and improves into the high band once a live tradable price path exists again.
